skills_considered.reason: A single re-analysed case with DNA-only evidence; nothing to mine beyond the patient-count record.
Scientists do not touch the four current files.
A reader cannot audit their own locators.

group_assessment.weighting: A paediatric genetics and CP-referral network re-analysing exome/genome data with deep phenotyping. Credible on re-analysis yield; no functional data for WWOX.

field_density.note: LEGEND holds no record of this paper; it holds two other sources of homozygous p.Leu239Arg (PAPER 013, PAPER 145) under a counting caution, and queues Serin 2018 (PMID 30094525).

multihop.disposition: 49 references enumerated from the JATS ref-list; none is a WWOX gene-direct reference (earned null). The paper cites no prior report of p.Leu239Arg although it applies PP5.

entries.proposition: Table 2 reports the WWOX case as homozygous for c.716T>G p.(Leu239Arg) with segregation from both parents, classified Pathogenic on PP3, PM3, PM2 and PP5 (PP5 = prior reputable report), annotated to both DEE28 and SCAR12; the only measurement is DNA and segregation.

entries.proposition: The Discussion names WWOX only as an example of the epileptic-encephalopathy subgroup reached by reverse phenotyping; there is no WWOX-specific analysis.
The authors themselves list functional validation of clinically relevant variants as missing, and their phenotype data as retrospective and possibly incomplete.
entries.snippet: clinical and phenotypic data were collected retrospectively, and Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms were extracted from hospital-based records
